subject: Metering for resumed live streams and accounting for partial generations
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@safewayhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@safewayhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing on resumed streaming sessions / partial outputs

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Before we push this to procurement, we need one more thing: a short plain explanation of how charges are calculated for "resumed" streaming responses. Two scenarios have come up: when a network disconnect causes a client to reconnect mid-generation, and when a generation is intentionally truncated (partial output) and later resumed.

Specifically: do we get billed for the entire attempt, only completed tokens, or is there a prorated approach? Also, would Redwood consider a goodwill credit for a certain number of disconnect events during our pilot? Procurement is concerned about unpredictable token spikes.

Can you send something short that we can include in the SOW/PO?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Director, Product Integrations
Safeway Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@safewayhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing on resumed streaming sessions / partial outputs

Jordan —

Short answer up front: billing is token-based and we meter tokens emitted by the model. For streaming sessions that disconnect and later resume, we bill for tokens actually generated by the model across attempts. That said, there are nuances we typically include in contract language for pilots:

- Disconnects/reconnects: tokens generated during the failed or incomplete attempt are billed. However, for pilot customers we can include a one-time "disconnect buffer" — a small token credit pool applied to the first month to reduce noise from edge instability.
- Partial generations and resume: when a client truncates output and requests a resume, the resumed generation is billed for the additional tokens produced after the resume point. We do not double-bill previously emitted tokens if the client references them as context.
- Retries with identical prompts: we meter per-server generation. If a client re-issues the same prompt and duplicates tokens, those duplicated tokens are billed. For deterministic retry logic (client-side dedupe) we recommend idempotency keys to avoid accidental double-billing.

I'll loop in Marissa and Sean for pricing/credit framing and have Prio(m) send example logs that show how tokens are counted for a resumed session. Attaching our standard ratecard for reference.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify billing on resumed streaming sessions / partial outputs

Jordan — quick pricing context:

- Baseline: hosted streaming is priced per 1K input tokens / 1K output tokens (see attached ratecard). Streaming mode itself has no premium beyond per-token rates.
- Pilot credits: for pilot agreements < 3 months we typically offer either a $5K platform credit or an equivalent token pool. In your case, we can structure the pilot credit to absorb the first ~450K output tokens (this is an example and can be tuned).
- Disconnect buffer: we can include a one-off 5% adjustment credit for the first 30 days to account for client-side instability if you include a clause to report disconnect incidents within 7 days. This is limited and intended to avoid open-ended exposure.
- Discounts: standard entry-level pilot discounts apply; larger committed monthly spends (Dedicated or annual) qualify for additional tiered discounts.

If you want, we can add explicit language in the SOW: "Redwood will apply a one-time pilot credit equal to X tokens to offset charges resulting from network disconnects documented within the first 30 days."

Would you like me to draft that sentence for the PO?

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success (Sales Ops)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@safewayhealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify billing on resumed streaming sessions / partial outputs

Jordan —

Attaching a short example from our logs to show how we attribute tokens when a streaming session disconnects and later resumes. Note: these are obfuscated IDs, not PII.

Summary of behavior (technical):

- Each streaming session is assigned a session_id and generation_id. Tokens emitted are recorded against the generation_id.
- If a disconnect occurs and the client reconnects and resumes the same generation_id, new tokens are appended to that generation and billed once.
- If the client starts a new generation (new generation_id) to "resume" by replaying prior tokens as prompt, the billing will include both the previously emitted tokens (if re-generated) and the new tokens.
- Retries: if a client retries the same API call without an idempotency key, the server treats it as a new generation and bills accordingly.

Attached: session-logs-20270508.txt — shows an example where a client disconnected at token 1,472 and reconnected; resumed generation appended +328 tokens (total billed 1,800 tokens for that generation).

Recommendations to avoid surprise charges:
- Use idempotency keys for retry-safe behavior.
- When resuming, use the same generation_id/session_id if you want resumed tokens merged into the same billed generation.
- Instrument client-side dedupe to avoid accidental replay of complete responses.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the logs.

—Priyom
Applied ML / Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: session-logs-20270508.txt (TXT, 12KB)]

Thanks — that is helpful and exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple follow-ups before I draft the PO:

1) Can Safeway Health request the 5% disconnect buffer for our first 30 days and have that documented in the SOW? If so, can you provide the exact Wording we should copy into the PO so procurement doesn't send it back with redlines?
2) For the pilot credit: instead of a dollar credit can we get a token pool defined (and a conversion table) so we can model it against our expected usage?

If you send bullet wording for the SOW (and a simple token->USD conversion for the ratecard attached), I can get procurement to move quickly. Also would you be open to a short 30-minute sync tomorrow to finalize?

Jordan
